starter.alt: The current street-team analysis starts with supplied fictional Forms inputs and an uncalculated Decision summary. Calculate and View decision process sit above the inputs.
starter.caption: Start analysis preserves supplied starter facts. Set two callouts, apply the change and calculate to reproduce Alex’s five-staff case.

financial.alt: The current Decision summary compares all four complete deployments: holding and the $200 one-person promotion meet operating requirements; five additional guests cover the one-person expense and six exceed it.
financial.caption: Read the operating answer and financial hurdles together. Two deployments fit the five-staff case; choosing the $200 push remains Alex’s management decision.

fiveStaff.alt: The current operational answer establishes two deployments that meet the recorded requirements when five qualified staff are available.
fiveStaff.caption: Five available: holding or sending one meets the recorded requirements. No profit-maximizing deployment is established.

process.alt: The street-team Decision process graph connects staffing and operating requirements to feasible deployments and a separate expense-recovery guest hurdle, with current-case and reassessment paths.
process.caption: The connected graph keeps operating eligibility and the financial guest hurdle separate. Highlighted paths describe responses available in Alex’s five-staff case; they record no dispatch or spending authorization.

pending.alt: Three unavailable staff are applied in Forms. The Decision summary says Recalculate the changed inputs rather than reusing the earlier operating answer.
pending.caption: Applying the third callout changes the basis. The summary withdraws the previous answer until the current staffing is recalculated.

fourStaff.alt: After the third callout, the current Decision summary establishes that only holding meets the recorded operating requirements.
fourStaff.caption: Four available: everyone is needed inside. Only holding meets the requirements.

thirdCallout.alt: The current Decision summary blocks all outreach deployments at four available staff while retaining their separate financial guest hurdles.
thirdCallout.caption: Recalculation makes the operating answer current. A five-guest financial target cannot supply the missing person.

financialReport.alt: The current Supporting reports, Expense recovery view displays the one-person plan’s $200 expense, $40 contribution, five guests to break even and six to exceed it, with its contribution and calculation details available.
financialReport.caption: Inspect the financial hurdle and open its supporting assumptions. These are the original $40 inputs; no promotion response has been measured.

comparison.alt: The current native comparison lists four deployments, additional expenses and the additional guests needed to cover and exceed each cost.
comparison.caption: All four financial hurdles remain visible for comparison. Guest counts describe required response rather than predicted attendance.

excelCoverage.alt: The optional Work with Excel disclosure offers workbook download and upload for the exact installed calculation workflow.
excelCoverage.caption: Excel supplies another route to the same case inputs. Apply the intended change, then recalculate.

processDetail.alt: The selected street-team feasibility question shows the current operating finding and the paths toward reviewing supported deployments or revising the plan.
processDetail.caption: Inspect the operating question to see why holding or sending one is supported. Its finding does not predict guest response or authorize a deployment.
